title: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit
body: Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat World Africa Asia Australia Europe Latin America Middle East Kyiv bridge hit in further Russian drone attack as German chancellor makes surprise visit Image source, AFP via Getty Images Image caption, A hole in the concrete road on the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge, which was hit by a Russian drone on Sunday By Ella Kipling and Jaroslav Lukiv Published 4 October 2026, 09:48 BST Updated 47 minutes ago Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by Russian drone strikes for four consecutive days, as Moscow ramps up attacks on critical infrastructure in Ukraine's capital. Two people were injured when the Pivnichnyi (Northern) Bridge was struck on Sunday morning for the second day in a row, while the Pivdennyi (Southern) Bridge was hit multiple times earlier in the week. The latest attack came as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv in a show of support against Russia's continuing full-scale invasion. Russia's military said it would be intensifying strikes on Kyiv and other Ukrainian regions. It earlier said it had hit the two bridges used to transfer Ukrainian troops. Video footage of Sunday's strike, verified by the BBC, shows cars moving on Pivnichnyi Bridge as a drone crashes into it before exploding, creating a ball of fire. A cloud of black smoke can be seen rising above the bridge. Other videos and pictures have emerged on social media showing a gaping hole in the middle of a traffic lane on the bridge. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said two people were injured in the latest Russian attack. He earlier said that the Pivnichnyi Bridge's roadway was hit. Kyiv's eight bridges across the wide Dnipro River link the western (right) and eastern (left) parts, and many of the capital's estimated three million residents rely heavily on the metro lines and trains to travel across the city. Some 500,000 vehicles use the bridges every day. The two struck bridges are still standing - but the damage and restrictions to traffic and public transport have caused gridlock in parts of the capital at times. "To get from the left bank to the right one and back - it's just hell," Kyiv resident Roman told the BBC on Sunday. Large numbers of commuters cross the river, especially on weekdays. Repair teams are working to fix the damage and officials say they are planning temporary pontoon bridges, ferry services and even a tunnel under the river to keep Kyiv connected. Klitschko also said a separate Russian drone strike had damaged a heating main, adding that there would be a temporary lack of hot water in the north-eastern Desnyanskyi district as a result. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenksy said on Sunday morning Russian drones had also attacked a warehouse in the north-eastern region of Sumy, killing one person. Meanwhile, in the central city of Dnipro, six people were injured after a communications facility was struck, he said. Ukraine's Air Force said that overnight Russia had launched 135 drones, including 52 jet-powered ones. It said that 125 projectiles had been shot down. As emergency services responded to the incidents, Germany's Merz met Zelenksy in Kyiv. They laid wreaths to Ukrainian soldiers who have been killed in the war. Merz reaffirmed his country's support for Ukraine, writing on X: "Ukraine is facing decisive weeks. That is why I travelled to Kyiv today with the message: You can rely on us. "Germany's security also depends on the outcome of this war. That is why we are helping out of our own self-interest as well." Image source, Reuters Image caption, Merz arrived in Kyiv by train Image source, Reuters Image caption, He joined Zelensky at a memorial to fallen Ukrainian soldiers Since Merz became chancellor in May 2025, Germany has become the single largest donor to Ukraine. He said the country "needs all our support in the coming weeks", adding: "If Russia is not stopped, its war machine will sooner or later turn against us." Zelensky said there would be "important agreements" made between Ukraine and Germany. The Ukrainian president has made repeated appeals for Western allies to provide more military support to the country, including supplying advanced interceptors that can shoot down new jet-powered Russian drones and also ballistic missiles. The Russian defence ministry said on Sunday it would intensify its strikes across Ukraine in response to comments made by Zelensky earlier this week, in which he said Kyiv would ramp up its attacks on Russian oil refineries. Russian President Vladimir Putin had earlier said his military was carrying out retaliatory attacks following Ukraine's strikes on Moscow's energy facilities, despite the fact that it was the Kremlin that had first launched such attacks. Putin began a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory. The Russian foreign ministry on Saturday repeated a warning for foreign citizens, including diplomats, to leave Kyiv. Responding to the warning, EU ambassador Katarína Mathernová wrote on X on Sunday: "The EU Delegation is staying. Threatening us will not stop Europe's support for Ukraine. It only reminds us why that support matters!" German ambassador to Ukraine, Boris Ruge, reacted to Mathernova's post with: "Amen - we're staying". Image source, Reuters Image caption, In Friday's attack, a Russian drone hit cables of Kyiv's Pivdennyi bridge Earlier attacks on the Pivdennyi Bridge prompted Kyiv's defence council to hold a crisis meeting on Friday. Klitschko warned that the city was now in a "very dramatic situation" as Moscow was battering its "critical infrastructure, logistics, housing" and other key facilities. Experts say Russian drones are unlikely to bring down the bridges - but repeated attacks will force their closure and risk weakening their structure, making them unusable. title: Voting in Brazil's 2026 presidential election has begun, with polls showing Lula and Bolsonaro nearly tied
body: Brazil election: Lula and Bolsonaro neck and neck Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites Latest videos Latest audio Regions Africa Asia Europe Latin America Middle East North America Germany Topics Climate Equality Health Human Rights Migration Technology Categories Business Science Environment Culture Sports In focus Israel Ethiopia German politics Latest audio Latest videos Live TV Advertisement Politics Brazil Brazil votes in tight election between Lula and Bolsonaro Wesley Rahn with Reuters, AFP, AP Published 10/04/2026 Published October 4, 2026 last updated 10/04/2026 last updated October 4, 2026 Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right populist President Jair Bolsonaro, is taking on incumbent left-wing President Lula da Silva. Polls show the first round of voting will likely lead to a runoff. https://p.dw.com/p/5NiO9 Supporters of Lula da Silva lined the main avenue in Sao Paulo for a final rally on Saturday Image: Andre Penner/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Voting began in Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, with leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva seeking a fourth non-consecutive term and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro seeking to continue the right-wing populist movement started by his father, Jair Bolsonaro. Polls have predicted a tight race between the two leading candidates, with neither likely to win more than 50% of the vote to avoid a runoff that would take place on October 25. Lula and Bolsonaro wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday in Brazil's economic powerhouse state of Sao Paulo. Lula vows to 'defeat the far-right' The 80-year-old Lula capped off his campaign with a tour through the city of Sao Paulo, vowing to "defeat the far right ." Organizers said some 150,000 of Lula's supporters turned up for the rally in Brazil's largest city. Lula has campaigned on continuing his left-leaning Workers' Party platform, comprising welfare programs, state-funded development and income redistribution. "The people will have to choose between strengthening the democratic regime and barbarism ... between progress and backwardness," he said as he cast his ballot on Sunday. The 80-year-old Lula is seeking the presidency for a fourth and final time Image: Amanda Perobelli/REUTERS Bolsonaro calls for 'change' Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, has served as the Liberal Party's senator for Rio de Janeiro since 2019. On Saturday, he led a motorcycle parade through Sao Paulo's countryside cities of Santa Barbara d'Oeste and Americana. He also held up a portrait of his father, while the crowd shouted "mito" — a Portuguese word for "legend" that Jair Bolsonaro's supporters use to refer to him. Flavio Bolsonaro has said he would pardon his father if elected Image: Douglas Shineidr/AFP The right-wing Bolsonaro has campaigned on hardline security policies and tax cuts, emphasizing high cost of living under Lula, who he has slammed as "incompetent." "Brazil needs change," the son of the former president said as he cast his vote. "Brazil cannot bear any more suffering, such as high taxes, so many women killed." Brazil's 2022 election rematch The elder Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year sentence in prison for attempting a coup to overturn his loss to Lula in the 2022 presidential election. Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed to pardon his father if elected. Lula's team has cast the Bolsonaro movement as a threat to Brazil's sovereignty, pointing to Flavio and Jair's ties with US President Donald Trump , who last year slapped a 50% tariff on Brazilian imports in response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial.  The US president called the case a "witch hunt." US President Trump had held close ties with fellow right-wing populist Jair Bolsonaro [FILE March 2019] Image: Chris Kleponis/CNP/MediaPunch/picture alliance The younger Bolsonaro has said in interviews he is "more moderate" than his father, who he has nevertheless said will remain "my compass, my point of reference." Policies where both Bolsonaros are similar include relaxed gun control laws and skepticism of human-caused climate change. Trump has not endorsed the senator, but has said he is watching the election "very closely." What happens next? Brazil finds itself politically divided, and campaigning has been bitter, with online operations from both sides seizing on every gaffe, accusation and rumor, quickly producing slick videos or AI-generated images for social media. In September, it was revealed Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion tied to the financing of a biopic about his father. He has denied any misconduct. Who is Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video The latest polling for the first round of voting shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45%, according to the Brazilian data intelligence and public opinion research firm Quaest cited by Reuters news agency. In the case of a run-off, the Quaest poll shows Lula at 42% and Bolsonaro at 44%. In 2022, Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro by only 1.8 percentage points. Along with voting for president, Brazil's 160 million registered voters are also choosing other lawmakers, governors, and some senators. title: Bosnia-Herzegovina votes amid divisive campaigns, EU bid
body: Bosnia-Herzegovina votes amid divisive campaigns, EU bid Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites Latest videos Latest audio Regions Africa Asia Europe Latin America Middle East North America Germany Topics Climate Equality Health Human Rights Migration Technology Categories Business Science Environment Culture Sports In focus Israel Ethiopia German politics Latest audio Latest videos Live TV Advertisement Politics Bosnia and Herzegovina Bosnia-Herzegovina votes amid divisive campaigns, EU bid Dharvi Vaid Dhulia with AFP, AP, DPA and Reuters 10/04/2026 October 4, 2026 Polls have opened in Bosnia and Herzegovina, where voters are taking part in parliamentary, presidential and local elections. https://p.dw.com/p/5Nim0 Preliminary results are expected to be available late Sunday after polls close Image: Armin Durgut/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement Polling began in Bosnia and Herzegovina on Sunday, with around 3.4 million voters eligible to take part in the Balkan country's general election. Citizens are electing officials across multiple tiers of government, including members of the multiethnic, tripartite presidency. They will also choose lawmakers for the federal parliament and the heads of institutions for the country's two largely autonomous entities —  the Muslim-Croat Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the Serb-run Republika Srpska. The election comes at a time when the country is struggling with a number of challenges. There's been an economic slowdown, sluggish progress toward EU membership, and a long-drawn-out political gridlock, with the ethnically based dominant parties from the two entities repeatedly stalling decisions by the weak central government that links them. The election will see adversary ethnic parties, the Bosniak ​SDA, Serb SNSD and Croat HDZ BiH, pitted against multi-ethnic opposition coalitions led by the Social Democratic Party. Polls close at 7 p.m. local time (1700 GMT), with preliminary results expected to be released late Sunday. What is the system that governs Bosnia-Herzegovina? The economic, administrative and political responsibilities in Bosnia and Herzegovina are divided between the multiethnic central government, the self-governing neutral Brcko district and the two semi-autonomous entities. Both entities are further split into several cantons and communities. The complicated framework — divided along ethnic lines — was set up during the US-brokered 1995 Dayton Peace Accords , following the 1992-95 Bosnian war which was triggered by the breakup of Yugoslavia. Simmering ethnic tensions Currently in Bosnia and Herzegovina's populace, around half are Muslim Bosniaks, while 31% are Orthodox Serb and 15% are Catholic Croat. The country has been peaceful in recent years but its ethnonationalist parties have kept the divisions alive even as voters say they want to move on from the war-era rhetoric and division. Milorad Dodik not on the ballot but still dominant in Republika Srpska In Republika Srpska , secessionist leader ​ Milorad Dodik of the SNSD party remains the key figure despite not being on the ballot. Dodik, the former president of the Serb-majority entity, is barred from holding public office for six years after being convicted of defying the top international envoy overseeing the 1995 peace process. Dodik-backed Savo Minic is running for the Republika Srpska's presidency. Dodik wants close ‌ties with Serbia and Russia. He has just returned from Moscow where he met Russian President Vladimir Putin. "Bosnia and Herzegovina is dead, it is an impossible country," Dodik told supporters at the final rally of his in Banja Luka on Friday. What is happening in the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina? In the Muslim-Croat federation, Bosniak parties are advocating for a stronger central state. The main Bosniak SDA party is focused on efforts to keep the country united against Serb separatism. Bosnian Croats are also largely backing their ethnic parties, including the Bosnian branch of Croatia's ruling conservative Croatian Democratic Union. Meanwhile, Denis Becirovic, the incumbent Bosniak presidency member, has vowed a renewed path to the EU and NATO. EU ambitions Bosnia and Herzegovina has been a candidate for EU membership since 2022. But the actual start of membership talks depends on the prior implementation of numerous reforms, including strengthening judicial oversight and passing anti-corruption ​laws. title: Yamal scores stunning goal in Spain’s 3-1 Nations League win over Czechia
body: Yamal scores stunning goal in Spain’s 3-1 Nations League win over Czechia | Football | Al Jazeera Skip links Skip to Content play Live Sign up Show navigation menu Navigation menu News Show more news sections Africa Asia US & Canada Latin America Europe Asia Pacific Middle East Explained Sport Opinion Video More Show more sections Originals Features Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up Sport | Football Yamal scores stunning goal in Spain’s 3-1 Nations League win over Czechia Lamine Yamal is the first player to score within the first 10 minutes of each of three consecutive men’s football games. Listen Listen (4 mins) Save Share Yamal’s sixth-minute stunner against Czechia helps Spain to a 3-1 win on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Lamine Yamal scored Spain's opening goal against Czechia during the UEFA Nations League Group A3 match at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium in Oviedo, Spain, October 3, 2026 [Miguel Riopa/AFP] By AFP Published On 4 Oct 2026 4 Oct 2026 Lamine Yamal has carried on his superb goal-scoring form, helping Spain secure a 3-1 win over Czechia in the UEFA Nations League and consolidating his bid to win the prestigious Ballon d’Or award later this month. The world champions moved three points clear of England at the top of Group A3 after Thomas Tuchel’s side demolished Croatia 7-0 earlier in Rijeka on Saturday. Spain cruised into a two-goal lead with Yamal and captain Rodri Hernandez on target, but Jiri Slama gave the Czechs a chance by pulling one back with 20 minutes to go. However, Mikel Merino wrapped up Spain’s win late on after Ladislav Krejci was sent off for the Czechs, as Spain racked up a 41st consecutive unbeaten game, including the World Cup final win over Argentina in July. Yamal, who scored in the second minute of Spain’s first two games against England and Croatia, waited as long as the sixth minute before breaking the deadlock. He is the first player to score a goal within the first 10 minutes of three consecutive men’s international matches. “They are well-drilled; I thought it would be one of the hardest games, and that’s how it was,” Rodri told a Spanish broadcaster after Spain claimed a third win from three group games. “It was tricky but we got some chances. There are some matches in which you can’t generate that much, but the team was able to manage the match.” The former Manchester City midfielder scored for the first time for Spain in more than two years. “It’s always special to score for the national team. I’d not been scoring many goals; let’s see if I’ve found that dynamic – it’s important, we all have to chip in with the goals,” he added. Advertisement Spain coach Luis de la Fuente made several changes in Oviedo from Tuesday’s win over Croatia, including handing debuts to full-back Ivan Fresneda and striker Roberto Fernandez. It was one of Spain’s star names, though, who lit up the game early on, something he is beginning to make a habit of. Yamal brings the ball down from a pass before going on to score a stunning goal [Miguel Riopa/AFP] The 19-year-old winger, a leading candidate for the Ballon d’Or, produced an exquisite finish from the right of the box, curling into the top corner after taking a touch to earn himself room to shoot. “We’re doing well; I’m very happy. I was eager to return to the national team after the World Cup, and there’s no better way than this,” said Yamal. Spain coach De la Fuente put his hands to his head in apparent shock at the quality of Yamal’s superb strike, his 12th in his last nine games for club and country. “I think he never stops surprising us – I think all of us. He has so much talent, so much quality, that we still haven’t seen the best version of Lamine by a long shot,” said De la Fuente. “He has a lot more to offer because he’s so classy, so talented, with so much potential.” The winger’s Barcelona teammate, Rodri, doubled Spain’s lead after 35 minutes, arriving in the box to drill into the top corner after the ball fell nicely for him. De la Fuente took off Yamal at half-time to give the young Barcelona star a break before Tuesday’s visit to face Croatia, and the pace of the game slowed. The Czechs pulled one back through Slama, who produced an excellent low finish across David Raya after Adam Hlozek played him in. Arsenal stopper Raya was fortunate a few minutes later when he conceded possession with a misplaced pass while out of his goal, but the visitors could not capitalise. Raya also spilled the ball badly and Ryan Naderi turned home, but the goal was disallowed for a foul on Robin Le Normand. Czechia’s determined efforts to battle back were derailed by Krejci’s red card, with the defender shown a second yellow for pulling back Fernandez, before Merino rounded off Spain’s win. aj-logo aj-logo aj-logo Advertisement About About Show more About Us Code of Ethics Terms and Conditions EU/EEA Regulatory Notice Privacy Policy Cookie Policy Cookie Preferences Accessibility Statement Sitemap Work for us Connect Connect Show more Contact Us User Accounts Help Advertise with us Stay Connected Newsletters Channel Finder TV Schedule Podcasts Submit a Tip Paid Partner Content Our Channels Our Channels Show more Al Jazeera Arabic Al Jazeera English Al Jazeera Investigative Unit Al Jazeera Mubasher Al Jazeera Documentary Al Jazeera Balkans AJ+ Our Network Our Network Show more Al Jazeera Centre for Studies Al Jazeera Media Institute Learn Arabic Al Jazeera Centre for Public Liberties & Human Rights Al Jazeera Forum Al Jazeera Hotel Partners Follow Al Jazeera English: facebook twitter youtube instagram-colored-outline rss bluesky tiktok-colored-outline © 2026 Al Jazeera Media Network

title: Australian authorities investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country
body: Australian authorities investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat World Africa Asia Australia Europe Latin America Middle East Australian authorities investigating Flydubai co-pilot's links to country Image source, Social Media Image caption, The Flydubai plane was diverted to Saudi Arabia after passengers managed to take back control from the co-pilot By Claire Keenan Published 11 minutes ago Australian authorities are investigating the links between the country and a Flydubai co-pilot who attempted to take control of a plane travelling to Israel. The co-pilot is alleged to have attacked the captain with a crash axe during a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv before passengers managed to overpower him and successfully take control of the plane. The Australian authorities have not identified the co-pilot, who has been named by multiple media outlets including Reuters, CNN and The New York Times as Hamam al-Hammami. The prosecutor in the UAE has said it is investigating the incident and any possible motives. In a statement to the BBC, the Australian Federal Police (AFP) confirmed its investigation into "the man's links to Australia". The investigation involves state police and the country's security agency, it said, adding that an update would be "provided at the appropriate time". Sources familiar with the case, who have spoken to Australian media, have said the co-pilot was issued a student visa in 2014, and studied in Australia between 2015 and 2017, until he left the country. The Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) said the co-pilot's student visa was cancelled in 2019 as he was no longer enrolled in a course, making him ineligible for it. Counter-terrorism officials will look at whether the man was radicalised in Australia, the ABC reported. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said he was an Omani national. The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv on 30 September was carrying more than 170 passengers to Israel. Two and a half hours into its journey, the plane plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) when the Omani co-pilot attacked the pilot with a crash axe , the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said. The pilot flying the plane, Capt Smit Machchhar, described how he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in. Two reserve pilots then landed the plane safely in Saudi Arabia. Figure caption, Watch: Flydubai pilot speaks with Indian PM Machchhar, and Indian national, was taken to a nearby hospital before being airlifted to Abu Dhabi, where he is reported to be in a stable condition. The co-pilot was arrested after the emergency landing and is being questioned by Saudi authorities, according to Netanyahu. The UAE's attorney general, Hamad Saif Al Shamsi, said on Saturday investigations were under way to establish the circumstances, motives and any links related to the incident. He said investigations into the incident revealed that the co-pilot attempted to carry out a "terrorist act", according to the country's state news agency. In the days since the attack more details have come to light about the co-pilot's employment history. While working at another airline, Oman Air, US media reported that Al-Hammami was removed from flight training because of concerns over his radical views, and was given another role at Oman's national airline. It is also known that, from 2020, he was studying on a distance-learning course run by Buckinghamshire New University in the UK. He graduated with a degree in aviation management in 2023, the university said. It added he did not take any pilot training at the school. title: West Indies beat India in record chase as Hope hits 162 in third ODI
body: West Indies beat India in record chase as Hope hits 162 in third ODI | Cricket | Al Jazeera Skip links Skip to Content play Live Sign up Show navigation menu Navigation menu News Show more news sections Africa Asia US & Canada Latin America Europe Asia Pacific Middle East Explained Sport Opinion Video More Show more sections Originals Features Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up Sport | Cricket West Indies beat India in record chase as Hope hits 162 in third ODI Shai Hope’s 162 leads the West Indies to a record cricket run chase as they beat India by five wickets in the third ODI. Listen Listen (4 mins) Save Share West Indies beat India in record chase as Hope hits 162 in third ODI on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info West Indies captain Shai Hope reacts after playing a shot during the third one-day international against India in Chandigarh on October 3, 2026 [Sajjad Hussain/AFP] By The Associated Press Published On 4 Oct 2026 4 Oct 2026 Captain Shai Hope’s unbeaten 162 led West Indies to a record run-chase win against India in one-day international cricket in Chandigarh. The West Indies achieved their highest ODI run chase on Saturday, reaching 352-5 and winning by five wickets with 10 balls to spare after India made 351-7, featuring Lokesh Rahul’s 129 not out. Recommended Stories list of 4 items list 1 of 4 Fernandes calls Ronaldo and denies Portugal rift ahead of Norway game list 2 of 4 ‘Verbal attack’: Israeli reporters interrupt Ireland news conference list 3 of 4 Ronaldo-less Portugal host Haaland’s Norway in Nations League list 4 of 4 Man City whistleblower Pinto says he ‘received death threats’ over leaks end of list India had already won the three-match series after eight-wicket wins in Thiruvananthapuram and Guwahati. But the West Indies, chasing for the first time in the series, overcame India for the first time since 2023. Hope promoted himself to opening batter after Jewel Andrew reportedly injured a finger making a catch and had to go to hospital. After keeping wicket for all of India’s 50 overs in high humidity, he batted brilliantly to score his second successive hundred in the series but struggled in the last overs. Fittingly, he hit the winning run. “Felt something around the groin area but wanted to fight through till the end,” Hope said. His second-highest ODI score, from 143 balls, included 17 boundaries and three sixes. Amir Jangoo added 67 off 56 and Keemo Paul 44 off 35. “[Chasing is] always a lot easier in India, especially with the dew,” Hope said. “Glad we got over the line.” Hope and Jangoo added 109 off 99 balls for the second wicket to defy an India bowling attack that recalled Mohammed Siraj and all-rounder Nitish Reddy and included debutant pacer Anshul Kamboj, who went wicketless. Jangoo was run out in the 21st over, but Sherfane Rutherford (24) did not let the momentum slip. He added 56 with Hope, who reached 50 off 46 balls and 100 off 104 in his 21st ODI hundred and fifth against India. Advertisement Paul’s cameo included five fours as he added 65 off 61 balls with his skipper. Hope shifted gears after Paul was dismissed in the 41st over, caught off Gurnoor Brar. Hope hit seven more fours and two sixes after his milestone, taking 62 off the last 39 balls faced to rush West Indies to victory. India had to serve a slow over rate penalty for the last four overs, with an additional fielder inside the 30-yard circle, as Hope and Gudakesh Motie (19 not out) added 62 off 29 balls for the sixth wicket. India won the toss again but skipper Shubman Gill was caught behind on 1 and Virat Kohli was bowled for a golden duck. Both fell to Jayden Seales. Only 28 runs came in the first 10 overs, then Rohit Sharma and Rahul propelled the hosts. Sharma resurrected the innings with 92 off 85 balls, adding 137 for the third wicket with Ruturaj Gaikwad. Sharma took his time and was unlucky to miss a second consecutive hundred in the series; he was caught off Paul in the 25th over. Four overs later, Gaikwad — 57 off 69 — was Seales’s third wicket. That brought Rahul to the crease, and he led the charge past 350. Rahul hit six sixes and 10 fours. He scored 50 off 41 balls and his second 50 off 39 balls. He enjoyed good partnerships with Naman Dhir and Brar and finished 129 not out off only 87 balls. The teams begin a five-match Twenty20 series on Tuesday, starting in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. aj-logo aj-logo aj-logo Advertisement About About Show more About Us Code of Ethics Terms and Conditions EU/EEA Regulatory Notice Privacy Policy Cookie Policy Cookie Preferences Accessibility Statement Sitemap Work for us Connect Connect Show more Contact Us User Accounts Help Advertise with us Stay Connected Newsletters Channel Finder TV Schedule Podcasts Submit a Tip Paid Partner Content Our Channels Our Channels Show more Al Jazeera Arabic Al Jazeera English Al Jazeera Investigative Unit Al Jazeera Mubasher Al Jazeera Documentary Al Jazeera Balkans AJ+ Our Network Our Network Show more Al Jazeera Centre for Studies Al Jazeera Media Institute Learn Arabic Al Jazeera Centre for Public Liberties & Human Rights Al Jazeera Forum Al Jazeera Hotel Partners Follow Al Jazeera English: facebook twitter youtube instagram-colored-outline rss bluesky tiktok-colored-outline © 2026 Al Jazeera Media Network

Here’s a quick guide to the voting process, candidates and what’s at stake. Listen Listen (7 mins) Save Share Bosnia’s high-stakes election: Here’s what to know on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info A man walks beneath an election poster featuring People and Justice Party (NiP) candidates for the upcoming general elections in Sarajevo, Bosnia on September 29, 2026 [Armin Durgut/AP Photo] By Kerim Sefer Published On 4 Oct 2026 4 Oct 2026 Bosnians are heading to the polls to choose the next government at all three of the state, entity and canton levels. It may seem complicated, but for a country divided into two entities – the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Republika Srpska, along with Brcko District – this is nothing new. When do Bosnia’s elections take place? The general elections are scheduled for Sunday, October 4. More than 3.4 million people are eligible to vote. [Al Jazeera] What’s different about this election? This year, new election technology will be used. Voters will be identified using biometric devices, while ballot papers will be scanned rather than simply placed in ballot boxes. The use of scanners, however, does not mean voting will be fully electronic. Votes will still be cast and recorded on paper, but verification and counting should be faster and more transparent, while voter identification should be more accurate. Who is running for the Presidency? Candidates for the Bosniak representative include current Presidency member Denis Becirovic of the Social Democratic Party (SDP), Bakir Izetbegovic of the Party of Democratic Action (SDA), Semir Efendic of the Party for Bosnia and Herzegovina (Stranka za BiH), and Fahrudin Radoncic of the Union for a Better Future of BiH (SBB). Izetbegovic, the president of the centre-right SDA, the biggest Bosniak party in the country, is running for his third term after being defeated by Becirovic in 2022. Three candidates will run for the Croat seat in the Presidency: Darijana Filipovic of the Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina (HDZ BiH), Slaven Kovacevic of the Democratic Front (DF), and Zdenko Lucic, a candidate supported by a coalition of five Croat parties. Advertisement The current Serb member of the Presidency, Zeljka Cvijanovic from the right-wing Alliance of Independent Social Democrats (SNSD), is running for a second term. During her term on the country’s top state body, which began in November 2022, just a few months after Russia’s war in Ukraine started, she maintained close and continuous cooperation with Russia and its president, Vladimir Putin. SNSD is led by Milorad Dodik, the former president of Republika Srpska, best known for his separatist moves and for challenging the Constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina and the decisions of former High Representative Christian Schmidt. Cvijanovic will face Marinko Bozovic of the Serb Democratic Party (SDS) and Nebojsa Vukanovic of the List for Justice and Order. [Al Jazeera] Who else is on the ballot? Voters will be choosing representatives for 14 governments, as well as members of the country’s three-member Presidency. Each entity has its own president, assembly, prime minister and ministers. The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina is further divided into 10 cantons, each with its own government. For all this to happen, the Central Election Commission (CIK), the main body responsible for overseeing the voting process, earlier said that 75 political parties and four independent candidates were registered and eligible to participate. How are Presidency members chosen? When registered voters go to the polls, they do not elect one president, but choose one of three members of the country’s collective head of state. They are the representatives of the three constituent peoples – Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs. The Bosniak and Croat members are elected from the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, while the Serb member is elected from Republika Srpska. This is because the majority of Bosniaks and Croats live in the Federation, while most Serbs live in Republika Srpska. The election of the Croat member has weighed on Bosniak-Croat relations for years and has often been used as a reason for political blockades. Parties gathered around the centre-right Croatian Democratic Union of Bosnia and Herzegovina (HDZ BiH) are demanding changes to the Election Law, saying they want to prevent Bosniak voters from influencing the election of the Croat member of the Presidency. But that would also require changes to the Constitution, which allows all citizens in the Federation to choose whether they want to vote for the Bosniak or the Croat member. [Al Jazeera] What about citizens who live outside their constituent group’s voting area? A Serb living in the Federation, or a Bosniak or Croat living in Republika Srpska, who wants to run would not be able to do so, nor can they vote for those they consider to be their own representatives. Advertisement That is one of the many paradoxes of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s electoral system. How is the state-level government chosen? Citizens elect representatives to the Parliamentary Assembly, which consists of two houses. Forty-two representatives will be elected to the House of Representatives. Two-thirds are directly elected from the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and one-third from Republika Srpska. A quorum consists of a majority of all members elected to the House of Representatives. The second chamber – the House of Peoples – has 15 delegates and is elected indirectly through the institutions. It consists of Bosniaks, Croats and Serbs – five from each group. What happens with the entities? The election of entity-level authorities works somewhat differently. In Republika Srpska, citizens directly elect the National Assembly, as well as the entity president and vice presidents. They do not directly elect the government – it is confirmed by the National Assembly. In the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, citizens directly elect the House of Representatives of the Federation Parliament and the cantonal assemblies. Those cantonal assemblies then elect delegates to the Federation’s House of Peoples. The president of the Federation, the entity government and the cantonal governments are formed after the elections, through parliamentary majorities and political agreements. Why is it a challenge to form the government? It is difficult not only because the electoral system is complex, but also because of the lack of agreement among representatives of the three different ethnic communities. Frequent blockades and obstruction make decision-making difficult at all levels, even though many politicians invoke the politics of compromise. Elections in Bosnia and Herzegovina, therefore, are not only about who wins, but about whether a system designed to represent everyone can serve its citizens. Why are the elections important? New election technologies might reduce potential fraud, but much more will be needed for the country’s path towards the European Union. The outcome of the election could unblock, or further slow down, the adoption of key laws needed for the country’s progress towards EU membership. The EU granted Bosnia and Herzegovina candidate status in December 2022 and opened accession negotiations in 2024. However, the country’s progress has since been assessed as very limited and slowed by political blockades. These elections will also be a test for the ruling coalition, which promised to focus on social and economic issues amid the rising cost of living. When are the results? The first preliminary results are traditionally published by CIK late on election night, on October 4, and are updated every few hours. In the days after the elections, CIK gradually enters votes from the remaining polling stations, mobile voting teams, as well as ballots received by mail and from diplomatic and consular missions. The official results will be known no later than November 20. aj-logo aj-logo aj-logo Advertisement About About Show more About Us Code of Ethics Terms and Conditions EU/EEA Regulatory Notice Privacy Policy Cookie Policy Cookie Preferences Accessibility Statement Sitemap Work for us Connect Connect Show more Contact Us User Accounts Help Advertise with us Stay Connected Newsletters Channel Finder TV Schedule Podcasts Submit a Tip Paid Partner Content Our Channels Our Channels Show more Al Jazeera Arabic Al Jazeera English Al Jazeera Investigative Unit Al Jazeera Mubasher Al Jazeera Documentary Al Jazeera Balkans AJ+ Our Network Our Network Show more Al Jazeera Centre for Studies Al Jazeera Media Institute Learn Arabic Al Jazeera Centre for Public Liberties & Human Rights Al Jazeera Forum Al Jazeera Hotel Partners Follow Al Jazeera English: facebook twitter youtube instagram-colored-outline rss bluesky tiktok-colored-outline © 2026 Al Jazeera Media Network

body: Houthis claim strike on Aramco site as Yemen fighting intensifies | Houthis News | Al Jazeera Skip links Skip to Content play Live Sign up Show navigation menu Navigation menu News Show more news sections Africa Asia US & Canada Latin America Europe Asia Pacific Middle East Explained Sport Opinion Video More Show more sections Originals Features Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up Navigation menu caret-left Iran Iran’s ‘axis’ in disarray Will Gulf states join war? Iran’s weapons Who's in charge in Iran? caret-right News | Houthis Houthis claim strike on Aramco site as Yemen fighting intensifies Spokesman for Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government says the Houthi claims of targeting Riyadh are ‘misleading’. Listen Listen (2 mins) Save Share Houthis claim strike on Aramco site as Yemen fighting intensifies on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Flames are seen at a facility belonging to Saudi oil giant Aramco, south of Riyadh, on October 3, 2026 [AFP] By Al Jazeera Staff Published On 4 Oct 2026 4 Oct 2026 | Updated: 6 hours ago Updated: 6 hours ago Yemen’s Houthis have said they attacked an Aramco facility in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, as fighting between the Iran-aligned group and Yemen’s Saudi-backed internationally recognised government intensifies. In a statement posted on X on Saturday, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group had carried out a “military operation with ballistic missiles and drones” that targeted Aramco in Riyadh. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 Are Houthis using new modified cruise missiles in Yemen’s war? list 2 of 3 Yemen’s war disrupts roads and ports, deepening humanitarian crisis list 3 of 3 Saudi Arabia not to compromise on security as Houthis choose ‘chaos’: MBS end of list He claimed the strikes were “precise and direct” and “led to fires breaking out” at the site. A large plume of smoke and fire was seen rising near an Aramco facility in Riyadh on Saturday. Later on Saturday, Turki al-Maliki, spokesman for the Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s government, said in remarks carried by Saudi media that the Houthi claims of targeting Riyadh were “misleading”. Early on Sunday, the Saudi-led coalition said its armed forces carried out 97 “precise targeting operations” against Houthi reinforcements on the Tor al-Baha front and the Taiz axis, using warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles and snipers. Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili, the spokesman for Yemen’s government forces, said the attacks targeted “at least 260 Houthi fighters and destroyed or disabled 44 military vehicles”. Late last month, the Houthis said they had attacked Aramco facilities in Yanbu, a Red Sea port on Saudi Arabia’s west coast. Saudi Arabia said at the time it intercepted six ballistic missiles fired towards Taif and Yanbu and reported no damage to Aramco sites. Earlier this week, the Saudi-led coalition said the Houthis attacked a power station in the Muslim holy city of Medina on Tuesday. Advertisement The fighting has intensified since a fragile 2022 truce collapsed in July. In mid-September, the Houthis seized the port city of Mocha and strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandeb strait, a vital route for global oil shipments, before anti-Houthi forces stabilised front lines. Hundreds of thousands of people have been displaced since fighting restarted. title: Peru: Fire burning on road to Machu Picchu kills 1
body: Peru: Fire burning on road to Machu Picchu kills 1 Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites Latest videos Latest audio Regions Africa Asia Europe Latin America Middle East North America Germany Topics Climate Equality Health Human Rights Migration Technology Categories Business Science Environment Culture Sports In focus Israel Ethiopia German politics Latest audio Latest videos Live TV Advertisement Nature and Environment Peru Peru: Fire burning on road to Machu Picchu kills 1 Dharvi Vaid Dhulia with AFP and LUSA 10/04/2026 October 4, 2026 One person has died and two others have suffered burns in a fire near the main access route to the historic sanctuary of Machu Picchu. https://p.dw.com/p/5NiW0 The Incas built Machu Picchu in the 15th century Image: Laurent Davoust/Zoonar/picture alliance Advertisement A blaze was burning near the main access road to the ancient Inca citadel of Machu Picchu in Peru , leaving one person dead and two injured, officials said on Saturday. The fire began on Friday in the Sacred Valley of the Cusco region, which also includes the Ollantaytambo train station — the busiest for travelers visiting Machu Picchu. "We have one elderly person who died in the flames and two others with second-degree burns," Miguel Osco, head of the Cusco Regional Office for Disaster Management and Safety, told RPP radio. How did the fire start? Osco said the fire originated from controlled bush burning that farmers carry out to clear land for crops. The flames spread quickly because of the hot, windy weather and dry vegetation, he added. The Incas built Machu Picchu in the 15th century. Located at an altitude of 2,500 meters in the Andes Mountains, the historic sanctuary is regarded as an architectural masterpiece . UNESCO designated it a World Heritage Site in 1983. Machu Picchu is Peru's most famous tourist destination, attracting about three million visitors every year. title: Brazil's 2026 presidential election is kicking off with polls showing Lula and Bolsonaro nearly tied.
body: Brazil election: Lula and Bolsonaro neck and neck Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites Latest videos Latest audio Regions Africa Asia Europe Latin America Middle East North America Germany Topics Climate Equality Health Human Rights Migration Technology Categories Business Science Environment Culture Sports In focus Israel Ethiopia German politics Latest audio Latest videos Live TV Advertisement Politics Brazil Brazil election: Polls show Lula and Bolsonaro neck and neck Wesley Rahn with Reuters, AFP, AP 10/04/2026 October 4, 2026 Flavio Bolsonaro, the son of former far-right populist President Jair Bolsonaro, is taking on incumbent left-wing President Lula da Silva. Polls show the first round of voting will likely lead to a runoff. https://p.dw.com/p/5NiO9 Supporters of Lula da Silva lined the main avenue in Sao Paulo for a final rally on Saturday Image: Andre Penner/AP Photo/picture alliance Advertisement The latest polling points to a tight race in Brazil's presidential election on Sunday, with leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva seeking a fourth non-consecutive term and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro seeking to continue the right-wing populist movement started by his father, Jair Bolsonaro. The two leading candidates wrapped up their campaigns on Saturday in Brazil's economic powerhouse state of Sao Paulo. Lula vows to 'defeat the far-right' The 80-year-old Lula capped off his campaign with a tour through the city of Sao Paulo, vowing to "defeat the far right," and framing the election as choice between "democracy and sovereignty" and "barbarism and corruption." Organizers said some 150,000 of Lula's supporters turned up for the rally in Brazil's largest city. Lula has campaigned on continuing his left-leaning Workers' Party platform, comprising welfare programs, state-funded development and income redistribution. The 80-year-old Lula is seeking the presidency for a fourth and final time Image: Amanda Perobelli/REUTERS Bolsonaro's law and order Flavio Bolsonaro, 45, has served as the Liberal Party's senator for Rio de Janeiro since 2019. On Saturday, he led a motorcycle parade through Sao Paulo's countryside cities of Santa Barbara d'Oeste and Americana. The right-wing Bolsonaro has campaigned on hardline security policies and tax cuts, emphasizing high cost of living under Lula, who he has slammed as "incompetent." Flavio Bolsonaro has said he would pardon his father if elected Image: Douglas Shineidr/AFP "I am convinced ​that everything is in place for us to win this election in the first round," the ​lawmaker said. He also held up a portrait of his father, while the crowd shouted  "mito" — a Portuguese word for "legend" that Jair Bolsonaro's supporters use to refer to him. Brazil's 2022 election rematch The elder Bolsonaro is currently serving a 27-year sentence in prison for attempting a coup to overturn his loss to Lula in the 2022 presidential election. Flavio Bolsonaro has vowed to pardon his father if elected. Lula's team has cast the Bolsonaro movement as a threat to Brazil's sovereignty, pointing to Flavio and Jair's ties with US President Donald Trump, who last year slapped a 50% tariff on Brazilian imports in response to Jair Bolsonaro's coup trial, which the US president called a "witch hunt." US President Trump had held close ties with fellow right-wing populist Jair Bolsonaro [FILE March 2019] Image: Chris Kleponis/CNP/MediaPunch/picture alliance The younger Bolsonaro has said in interviews he is "more moderate" than his father, who he has nevertheless said will remain "my compass, my point of reference." Policies where both Bolsonaros are similar include relaxed gun control laws and skepticism of human-caused climate change. Trump has not endorsed the senator, but has said he is watching the election "very closely." What happens next? Brazil finds itself politically divided, and campaigning has been bitter, with online operations from both sides seizing on every gaffe, accusation and rumor, quickly producing slick videos or AI-generated images for social media. In September, it was revealed Bolsonaro is under investigation for alleged corruption, money laundering and tax evasion tied to the financing of a biopic about his father. He has denied any misconduct. Who is Brazil's Flavio Bolsonaro? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Polls show neither candidate is likely to win more than 50% of valid votes on Sunday needed to avoid a runoff that would take place on October 25. The latest polling for the first round of voting shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45%, according to the Brazilian data intelligence and public opinion research firm Quaest cited by Reuters news agency. In the case of a run-off, the Quaest poll shows Lula at 42% and Bolsonaro at 44%. In 2022, Lula beat Jair Bolsonaro by only 1.8 percentage points. Along with voting for president, Brazil's 160 million registered voters are also choosing other lawmakers, governors, and some senators. title: Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations
body: Cornell University president says school 'must do better' after rape allegations  - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat US & Canada Cornell president says university 'must do better' after frat house rape allegations Image source, Getty Images Image caption, A student has alleged she was drugged and gang-raped inside the Chi Phi frat house at Cornell University By Toby Mann and Ana Faguy Published 4 October 2026, 00:35 BST Updated 01:11 BST Cornell University's president says the school "must do better" after a woman alleged she was drugged and raped by a group of men at a fraternity house. In an eight-minute video statement released on Saturday night, Michael Kotlikoff described the allegations raised by the woman, identified as Jane Doe, as "deeply disturbing". The alleged incident has raised questions around the culture on campus of drug and alcohol use, and the way investigations were conducted in the case, Kotlikoff said. Jane Doe was a 20-year-old student at the university when she says seven men from its Chi Phi fraternity assaulted her for hours in an incident involving alcohol and the drug ketamine on 19 October 2024. She said she had reported the incident two weeks after it happened to Cornell University police, which investigated, but no charges were laid. Last month, Jane Doe filed a civil lawsuit against the Ivy League university, in which she alleged Cornell had failed to protect her or adequately punish the men involved. Kotlikoff said Cornell was "committed to investigating" the way the case was handled, and said the school administration and community "must do better". "We must foster a culture in which sexual assault is inexcusable and ensure our community is empowered and understands informed consent," he said. He added that university leaders need to create an environment where victims of sexual assault "feel safe coming forward and are treated with compassion and dignity". Kotlikoff said it is a "defining moment" in the university's history. "We must lead the way, we owe it to Jane Doe and to survivors of assault to get this right. And we must keep each other safe," he said. On the university's campus this week, the BBC saw growing frustration about the situation. Figure caption, Cornell students voice frustration at public hearing over rape case At a public hearing for students to speak about the alleged gang rape, many told the BBC they were ashamed of what happened and said the university had failed Jane Doe. "Our administration needs to change and it needs to change drastically and it needs to change fast," one student told the BBC. "Something like this never should have happened, this is a disgrace." As part of "broader work" that needs to happen, Kotlikoff said in his video statement that there should be a "serious look at the role of fraternities and sororities in campus life". "Being part of a group can never diminish individual responsibility for our own actions, for how we treat others, or for speaking up when someone may be at risk," he said. The university president also said that at the "appropriate time", the school would speak about how Cornell will "use this moment, this conversation, this anger, to help lead the broader effort to combat sexual assault not only on our campus, but beyond it". New York Governor Kathy Hochul has said she was "deeply disturbed" by how the investigation was handled, and has appointed New York Attorney General Letitia James to lead a review of the case. Kotlikoff said he supported the decision to appoint James to lead a criminal investigation, and welcomed an independent review by a law firm of how Cornell has handled the matter. Jane Doe said in her lawsuit that she was intoxicated during the alleged incident and could not provide consent. title: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro close campaigns ahead of critical election
body: Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro close campaigns ahead of critical election | Elections News | Al Jazeera Skip links Skip to Content play Live Sign up Show navigation menu Navigation menu News Show more news sections Africa Asia US & Canada Latin America Europe Asia Pacific Middle East Explained Sport Opinion Video More Show more sections Originals Features Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up News | Elections Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro close campaigns ahead of critical election Latest polls suggest Lula’s lead over Bolsonaro is narrowing, with neither candidate likely to win outright on Sunday. Listen Listen (3 mins) Save Share Brazil’s Lula and Bolsonaro close campaigns ahead of critical election on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who is running for re-election, waves a Brazilian flag during a campaign rally in Sao Paulo on October 3, 2026, a day ahead of the country's general election [Andre Penner/AP] By Al Jazeera Staff , AFP and Reuters Published On 4 Oct 2026 4 Oct 2026 Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro have wrapped up their election campaigns, each voicing confidence in victory ahead of Sunday’s tightly contested first-round presidential vote. Lula, 80, closed his re-election bid on Saturday with a march through Sao Paulo, Brazil’s economic powerhouse, drawing what his campaign called a record crowd for a closing rally. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 A political dynasty? Why the Bolsonaro family dominates Brazil’s right wing list 2 of 3 Election debate cancelled in Brazil, bomb scare outside Supreme Court list 3 of 3 How the Banco Master scandal injected chaos into Brazil’s presidential race end of list “Tomorrow, we’re going to win the elections in the first round,” he told supporters, describing Sunday’s vote as a choice between “democracy and barbarism” and promising to “defeat the far right”. He has also framed the election as a test of Brazil’s sovereignty, warning against “meddling” by Washington. Bolsonaro led a motorcycle caravan through towns in Sao Paulo state, echoing the campaign style of his father, before rallying later in Rio de Janeiro. “I am convinced that everything is in place for us to win this election in the first round,” he said. The 45-year-old is the son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, a close ally of US President Donald Trump. The former leader, 71, is serving a 27-year prison sentence for attempting to overturn his 2022 election loss to Lula. The younger Bolsonaro was photographed at his rally holding a portrait of his father. Trump has not formally endorsed Bolsonaro but has said he is watching the election “very closely”, a level of US interest that has become a flashpoint in the campaign . Lula’s supporters have seized on it as evidence Washington is trying to meddle in the elections, while some Bolsonaro supporters, frustrated by the cost of living, say they would welcome US pressure if it helped force change at home. Polls released on Saturday suggested Lula was still ahead but his lead was narrowing, with neither candidate likely to win outright on Sunday. Such a result would send the race to a run-off on October 25 between the two frontrunners, a contest polls suggest would also be close. Advertisement It is a far tighter race than Lula’s last victory in 2022, when he beat the elder Bolsonaro by less than two percentage points. Meanwhile, the Bolsonaro campaign has faced scrutiny over a film-funding scandal. Flavio Bolsonaro is under investigation over financing for Dark Horse, a biopic about his father, bankrolled by a jailed banker tied to one of Brazil’s biggest financial scandals. Brazil’s Supreme Court authorised federal police in April to investigate whether Flavio Bolsonaro made defamatory statements about Lula. Bolsonaro has pledged to seek his father’s release from prison if elected, and has echoed his father’s unsubstantiated claims questioning the reliability of Brazil’s electronic voting system, which analysts say could be laying the groundwork to contest the result if he loses. Beyond the presidency, Brazil’s nearly 160 million registered voters will also choose lawmakers, governors and senators on Sunday. title: US father and son arrested after 'gas station heroin' deaths
body: Father and son smoke shop workers arrested in Mississippi students' suspected kratom deaths - BBC News BBC Homepage Skip to content Accessibility Help Your account Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds More menu More menu Search BBC Home News Sport Earth Reel Worklife Travel Culture Future Music TV Weather Sounds Close menu BBC News Menu Home Climate World US & Canada UK Business Tech Science Entertainment & Arts Health More In Pictures BBC Verify Newsbeat US & Canada Father and son smoke shop workers arrested in Mississippi students' suspected kratom deaths Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Kratom is legal in some states, including Mississippi Published 3 October 2026 A father and son who worked at a Mississippi smoke shop have been arrested and charged in connection with the death of at least one university student who died from a suspected overdose of kratom, sometimes called "gas station heroin" in the US. The pair worked at a shop that allegedly sold derivatives of the substance to  University of Mississippi students. US prosecutors charged Yahya Mohamed Mosleh, 51, and Islam Yahya Mosleh, 18, for possession with the intent to distribute controlled substances in connection with the death investigation of two Ole Miss students last month. Although their deaths have not officially been attributed to kratom, officials afterward issued warnings about consuming kratom . The criminal complaint alleges that on 21 September, an Ole Miss student was found dead in his dorm room. The apparent cause of death "appeared to be consistent with a drug overdose", the US Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Mississippi said in a press release. Law enforcement found packages - with some tablets missing - of suspected kratom derivatives. About an hour later, a second student was found dead from a suspected overdose in another location, also with packages of suspected kratom derivatives. Officials connected the packages with the local vape, tobacco and beer store, the US Attorney's statement said. Law enforcement executed search warrants and seized suspected kratom derivative controlled substances from the store. The Mosleh's, father and son, were later arrested. The two students' deaths have sparked alarm and warnings from officials about the plant-based drug referred to as "gas station heroin". Kratom - a herb with opioid-like effects - has grown in popularity in the US over the last decade, and is typically purchased over the counter and consumed in pill or liquid form. For years, anti-kratom advocates have pushed for bans, and in some countries, like the UK, it is illegal. But Kratom is not regulated by the US Food and Drug Administration and is legal in some states, including Mississippi. The Mississippi prosecutors said that kratom derivatives, such as MGPI, MGM-15 and MGM-16, are now schedule I controlled substances in the US and can be significantly more potent than natural kratom leaf products and morphine. title: AI giants 'not being nearly careful enough,' warns outgoing OpenAI safety engineer
body: AI giants not 'careful enough,' ex-OpenAI engineer warns Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites Latest videos Latest audio Regions Africa Asia Europe Latin America Middle East North America Germany Topics Climate Equality Health Human Rights Migration Technology Categories Business Science Environment Culture Sports In focus Israel Ethiopia German politics Latest audio Latest videos Live TV Advertisement Technology United States of America AI giants not 'careful enough,' ex-OpenAI engineer warns Nik Martin with AFP, Reuters 10/03/2026 October 3, 2026 Days after US President Donald Trump signed a voluntary pact with artificial intelligence giants, a former OpenAI worker said his industry needs the same safeguards as nuclear power or aviation. https://p.dw.com/p/5NiBc OpenAI has delayed plans for a public listing this year due to safety concerns Image: Samuel Boivin/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement A safety engineer who recently quit ChatGPT creator OpenAI warned Saturday that artificial intelligence (AI) firms were "not being nearly careful enough." David Robinson's comments come amid growing concerns about AI becoming too powerful — a threat that US President Donald Trump has labeled a "hoax." OpenAI and Anthropic recently disclosed cases in which their AI models slipped past safety controls, hid mistakes and hacked systems they were not meant to access. How US, China could end the AI race To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video What did David Robinson write? In an op-ed for The Atlantic , Robinson said AI needs guardrails similar to those for nuclear power and aviation, adding, "The time for trial and error is over." He called for more emphasis on safety and research before US Big Tech develops more advanced AI models "so that the occasional and inevitable human error does not open a door to disaster." Robinson, who oversaw safety reports for 12 frontier AI-model launches, said the recent errors were typical because tech giants are prioritizing "speed and flexibility." "An environment where things like this can happen is no place to grow artificial minds that could be smarter than we are and that might not do what we want them to." The former OpenAI employee noted that the firm relies on "iterative deployment." It releases new AI models first and only tightens safeguards after problems show up. "As ​the company sprints from one launch to the next, it is failing to achieve the ​level of care ‌that I believe is needed," Robinson, who worked at OpenAI for 3 1/2 years, added. Activists have staged protests calling on AI labs to slow development Image: Karl Mondon/AFP ChatGPT creator insists AI is safe OpenAI reacted to the latest criticism in a statement, "We're making sure our models don't become more capable than we can safely manage ​and secure, and ⁠we pause training or hold back models when we need to slow down." In recent months, there have been repeated warnings from technology experts and policymakers that AI models are advancing so fast they could take control and possibly wipe out humanity . Despite those fears, US President Donald Trump is vehemently against stronger regulation, insisting that it will slow down innovation and make it harder for US AI models to beat Chinese rivals. This week, Trump announced a voluntary safety pact with six companies — Nvidia, SpaceX, OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Alphabet's Google. The president described the deal as "morally binding,” even if it is not legally enforceable. He also directed his administration to rename AI as "Super Intelligence" or SI. A survey by Reuters/Ipsos last month found that three-quarters of Americans worry that AI giants are not doing enough to stop AI from causing serious harm to society. title: Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching
body: Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching | Donald Trump News | Al Jazeera Skip links Skip to Content play Live Sign up Show navigation menu Navigation menu News Show more news sections Africa Asia US & Canada Latin America Europe Asia Pacific Middle East Explained Sport Opinion Video More Show more sections Originals Features Economy Human Rights Climate Crisis Investigations Interactives In Pictures Science & Technology Podcasts Travel Sponsored Content play Live Click here to search search Sign up Navigation menu caret-left Donald Trump Trump, Netanyahu and the Iran question How Iran war fallout may shape US elections A visual guide to redistricting caret-right News | Donald Trump Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching The US president published a lawmaker’s cell phone number as he called for the passage of a bill making Daylight Saving Time permanent. Listen Listen (4 mins) Save Share Trump ramps up pressure on US Republicans to end US clock switching on social media share-nodes Share facebook x whatsapp-stroke copylink google Add Al Jazeera on Google info Donald Trump gestures to reporters at the White House on Friday [Jose Luis Magana/AP Photo] By Al Jazeera Staff and Reuters Published On 3 Oct 2026 3 Oct 2026 United States President Donald Trump has increased the pressure on US Senate Republicans to make Daylight Saving Time permanent, singling out one of the body’s members for stalling legislation to end the twice-a-year changing of clocks. In a social media post on Saturday, Trump blasted US Senator Tom Cotton for “holding up” the Sunshine Protection Act, which Trump has personally opted to call the “No More Changing of Clocks Act”. Recommended Stories list of 3 items list 1 of 3 ‘Inconvenient’: Trump aims to end ‘costly’ daylight saving time in the US list 2 of 3 What is daylight saving time and which countries are changing their clocks? list 3 of 3 Why can’t America agree on what time it is? end of list “For some reason, Tom is stopping the Bill and, in the Senate, it’s very easy to do, it only takes one!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social account about the Arkansas Republican. “It should pass overwhelmingly, in a Bipartisan fashion”. “Nobody wants to spend their precious time running all over the place, turning Clocks back twice a year and, having sunshine in the afternoon is better than early in the morning!” he added. Trump went even further, publishing what he claimed was Cotton’s phone number as he implored Arkansas residents to pressure him. The move echoed a moment during the 2016 Republican presidential primaries, when then-candidate Trump gave out US Senator Lindsey Graham’s number after the former rival criticised him. US Senator Tom Cotton speaks to reporters at the US Capitol in Washington [File: J. Scott Applewhite/AP Photo] Al Jazeera called the number listed in Trump’s post, but an automated message stated the voicemail box was full. Cotton’s spokesperson and the White House did not respond to requests for comment. The president has routinely pushed Senate Republicans to pass legislation mandating year-round daylight saving, which would end Americans’ decades-long practice of changing their clocks twice a year to increase daylight hours. On Friday, Trump urged the US Senate to approve the bill, which passed the US House in July by a 308-117 vote. Advertisement Cotton has previously opposed the bill, arguing in a US Senate floor speech last year that farmers, construction workers, commuters and children heading to school would begin their days in the dark during the winter. Trump disputed that argument in a separate post on Saturday, saying the bill “would be a very nice and easy WIN for the Republican Party”. “If Tom Cotton were putting Arkansas first, he would give them an extra hour of daylight and, more importantly, they wouldn’t have to run all over their houses, farms, workplaces, and everywhere else, twice a year, having to change their Clocks, and often forgetting to do so”, Trump wrote. Trump, an avid golfer, also highlighted what he considered to be another selling point of the bill: the North American Professional Golfers’ Association (PGA) tour. “The PGA TOUR, as an example, needs more Daylight in the afternoon in order to finish their Tournaments”, he wrote in a post, which included a letter from PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp supporting the bill. “Likewise, regular Golfers, Tennis Players, Hunters and, perhaps more importantly, Farmers who want more Daylight to play or work.” The US president, who spent part of Saturday at his golf club in Sterling, Virginia, indicated in a subsequent post that he had received personal feedback on the proposal: “I don’t know about anyone else, but a table full of very distinguished people just told me that they HATE, immediately after a mandatory time change, going home at night – and it’s DARK. It’s depressing!” In 1974, the US Congress briefly adopted year-round daylight saving time in response to the country’s energy crisis. But Congress repealed the law less than a year later over safety concerns as children commuted to school before sunrise. US senators left Washington this week and have no set plans to return until after the November 3 midterm elections. Some members, such as Senator John Kennedy, weren’t optimistic that Senate Republican Leader John Thune would bring the bill up for a vote before polling day. “It’s dead as disco,” the Louisiana Republican told Reuters this week of Trump’s push to make daylight saving time permanent. “My sense is it would have trouble passing … I don’t think the leader is going to bring it up.” aj-logo aj-logo aj-logo Advertisement About About Show more About Us Code of Ethics Terms and Conditions EU/EEA Regulatory Notice Privacy Policy Cookie Policy Cookie Preferences Accessibility Statement Sitemap Work for us Connect Connect Show more Contact Us User Accounts Help Advertise with us Stay Connected Newsletters Channel Finder TV Schedule Podcasts Submit a Tip Paid Partner Content Our Channels Our Channels Show more Al Jazeera Arabic Al Jazeera English Al Jazeera Investigative Unit Al Jazeera Mubasher Al Jazeera Documentary Al Jazeera Balkans AJ+ Our Network Our Network Show more Al Jazeera Centre for Studies Al Jazeera Media Institute Learn Arabic Al Jazeera Centre for Public Liberties & Human Rights Al Jazeera Forum Al Jazeera Hotel Partners Follow Al Jazeera English: facebook twitter youtube instagram-colored-outline rss bluesky tiktok-colored-outline © 2026 Al Jazeera Media Network
